races.title: State Senate, District 23
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Jonah Garson
cands.bio: Chapel Hill attorney and longtime Democratic organizer. Appointed to the North Carolina Senate (District 23: Caswell, Orange and Person counties) in April 2026. Former First Vice Chair of the NC Democratic Party and Orange County Democratic Party chair. Worked for state legislators, the NY Attorney General's Labor Bureau, Milbank and Parry Law.

controversies.text: In February 2025, days before a party officer vote, an unsigned email to Democratic Party leaders claimed, without evidence, that Garson used cocaine at party events. Garson said he has never used cocaine and called the claim false and defamatory. No court or official finding was reported. He was re-elected vice chair with 59%.

Video of Garson being removed from a Chapel Hill bar in 2024 circulated in 2025. Garson says he confronted the bartender over alleged underage drinking. The bartender says that accusation was false. Three state senators cited the incident when raising concerns about his 2026 appointment. No official finding was reported.

cands.gaps: No bills he sponsored or other official actions in office were found, because he has served only since April 2026 and the sponsored-legislation list on his Ballotpedia page was empty. His campaign issues page was cut off partway, so his stated positions on housing, public safety and policing, gun violence, conservation and environment, and the state budget could not be read. No statements on data centers or on development and growth were found. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so his answers there are from his 2022 House race. No endorsements from notable organizations were found; Ballotpedia lists only individual-run voter-guide groups.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia and Wikipedia say he was born in Chapel Hill, and his campaign site says he was raised there and graduated from Chapel Hill High School in 2005.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Attorney for over 10 years (NY Attorney General's Labor Bureau, Milbank, Parry Law in Chapel Hill). Earlier worked for Sen. Ellie Kinnaird, Rep. Paul Luebke and Speaker Joe Hackney's campaign. State Senator since April 2026. Chaired the Orange County Democratic Party and was First Vice Chair of the state party.
qual.why: Legal career plus years of legislative staff work and now service in the Senate fit a law-and-budget job. Time in office is short (since April 2026), and he lost a 2022 House primary, so this is below the top of the range.
qual.label: Legal career plus years of legislative staff work and now service in the Senate fit a law-and-budget job. Time in office is short (since April 2026), and he lost a 2022 House primary, so this is below the top of the range.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site says he wants to end 287(g) agreements that let ICE use local law enforcement, and to abolish ICE and replace it with a new federal immigration agency.

clean-money.evidence: His campaign site says he wants to end Citizens United and take big money out of politics.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says he will work to defeat legislation undermining the right to choose and fight to guarantee abortion rights in the state constitution and repeal existing barriers to abortion.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised

roots.summary: Ballotpedia and Wikipedia say he was born in Chapel Hill, and his campaign site says he was raised there and graduated from Chapel Hill High School in 2005.

cands.name: Laura Pichardo
cands.bio: Accounts payable business analyst with an MBA, according to her campaign site. UNCG graduate. Treasurer of the Caswell County Republican Party 2022-2026. Ran for U.S. House (NC-6) in 2020 and 2022 and NC Senate District 23 in 2024 and 2026. No elected office is listed.
cands.gaps: We could not find where she grew up or when she moved to North Carolina. Her campaign site is the only source for her job history and her party treasurer role, and her Issues page was cut off partway through the education section. We found no statements from her on data centers, immigration or H-1B visas, guns, abortion, school vouchers or charters, or limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers. Her site mentions encouraging artificial intelligence and technology infrastructure but does not mention data centers. In a 2019 survey she said she did not want women punished for miscarriages, which is not a position on abortion restrictions. No endorsements were identified, and no news coverage or controversies were found. She has no voting record because she has not held office.

local.label: Roots 40: Ballotpedia says she was born in Greensboro, and the record shows her in North Carolina as an adult since graduating from UNC Greensboro in 2014 (about 12 years), with Caswell County party and advocacy work from 2020 on; where she grew up is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Accounts payable business analyst with nearly a decade in finance, business operations and technology implementation, plus small-business work (self-reported); holds an MBA; Caswell County Republican Party treasurer 2022-2026; no elected office found.
qual.why: She has a business and finance background relevant to budgeting but no legislative or local elected service, which puts her in the middle range.
qual.label: She has a business and finance background relevant to budgeting but no legislative or local elected service, which puts her in the middle range.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Says she will keep North Carolina affordable by protecting homeowners from excessive property taxes, supporting balanced budgets and reducing unnecessary government spending. She does not propose eliminating homestead taxes.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Lists protecting family farms and preserving agricultural land among her priorities. The same page also backs expanding water and sewer capacity and site development to attract new employers.

back-police-order.evidence: Says she supports public safety by ensuring law enforcement officers have the resources they need to protect communities.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says she will support competitive teacher compensation to recruit and retain educators. The page text I could read has no position on vouchers, charters or school choice.

prio.label: Matches 4 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 4 only promised
